distribution.title: The tax account freelancers skip
distribution.visual_hook: Phone in hand, banking app open, straight to camera
distribution.spoken_hook: Every freelancer I know is doing their taxes backwards. You are lending the government money for free.
distribution.belief: You are going to sort it out in April, when you can see the whole year.
distribution.script: You are going to sort it out in April, when you can see the whole year. Except by April the money is already spent, so the only lever left is a payment plan. I did that for three years running. Every quarter I priced the next job out of panic, because I did not know what I actually earned. The fix takes 10 minutes. Open a second account and name it Tax. Every time you get paid, move 25 percent in before you touch the rest. Now the scary number in April is already sitting there, and you can finally see what you earn.
distribution.directions: Punch in on the banking app when you say the word Tax. On-screen text at the 25 percent line: '25% of every invoice'. Hard stop on the last line, no outro.
distribution.value: Educational: a 10 minute second-account setup that removes tax panic for good.

Raising your rate is the worst first move for a struggling freelance business.

Fix collection speed, scope and concentration first. Then raise the rate from a position where you can afford a no.
